lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Lakeside Golf Club | Caddie | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Caddied about 5 rounds a week, carrying bags and reading greens for members.
- Helped the pro shop run the weekend junior tournament.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved close efficiency by 40% by automating reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Wrote the variance commentary for the monthly board pack, explaining each line more than 5% off budget.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Reported a 45% group EBITDA margin by adding the EBITDA margins of the three business units.
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Underwrote 60 small-business loans worth USD 45M, and none of the approved loans defaulted in their first two years.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Tested the valuation's sensitivity: a 1-point change in the discount rate moved the share value from USD 52 to USD 44.
- Shared the model and a two-page note with the university investment club, which used it in its spring pitch.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Built an 18-month cash forecast for a USD 600M business, holding error to about 4% and freeing USD 40M to repay debt early.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Bloomberg Terminal
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: The profile link may be a placeholder rather than a real, working professional profile.
items.because: Recruiters need working contact details.

items.says: “About” makes the five-round workload figure sound imprecise.
items.because: Keep the metric only if you can state it confidently.

items.says: The bullet could emphasize service or operational responsibilities more.
items.because: Those responsibilities may better support your target roles.

items.says: “Helped” does not show your specific responsibility.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what you owned.

items.says: The bullet does not indicate the tournament’s size.
items.because: A meaningful event measure would make the work more informative.

items.says: “Close efficiency” does not define what improved by 40%.
items.because: A tracked measure would make the result verifiable and meaningful.

items.says: The 40% improvement lacks a comparison period.
items.because: The result needs a basis for comparison.

items.says: Your contribution to the capital-plan model is unclear.
The bullet does not say what decisions or evaluations the model enabled.
Using the same discount rate for every project needs explanation.
items.because: It could suggest project risk was not considered.

items.says: The meaning of the 5% budget threshold is unclear.
items.because: It is not clear whether it means percentage variance against budget.

items.says: The scope of the 5% threshold is unclear.
items.because: It is not clear whether it applied to every line item or only material ones.

items.says: The bullet describes the task without showing the commentary’s usefulness or scope.
The valuation pairs FCFE with WACC.
items.because: FCFE is discounted at the cost of equity, not WACC.

items.says: Verify that the stated method matches the value produced.
items.because: The bullet should distinguish equity value from enterprise value.

items.says: Adding business-unit EBITDA margins does not produce a group EBITDA margin.
items.because: The group result must reflect the units’ EBITDA and revenue weights.

items.says: The USD 600M cash-flow forecast duplicates the Student Investment Fund bullet despite conflicting dates.
items.because: The two entries make the accomplishment look copied and chronologically implausible.

items.says: The forecast-error measure and period are undefined.
The link between the forecast and early debt repayment needs clarification.
items.because: The wording could imply that the forecast alone caused the full repayment.

items.says: The zero-default claim needs an observation period and a clear eligible loan group.
items.because: It should cover loans that completed the full two-year period.

items.says: The bullet should not imply that underwriting alone caused zero defaults.
items.because: Zero defaults does not prove that causal claim.

items.says: The size of the reviewed application population is missing.
items.because: It would provide context for the approval-rate change.

items.says: The period used to assess early defaults is missing.
items.because: It would support the claim of no rise in early defaults.

items.says: The claimed link between your findings and higher approvals needs substantiation.
items.because: “Raised approvals” implies a causal link.

items.says: The increase should be identified as seven percentage points rather than a 7% relative increase.
items.because: Those are different ways to describe the change from 41% to 48%.

items.says: “Writes” uses present tense for a completed role.
The before-and-after periods behind “7 to 1 a year” are unclear.
items.because: The comparison should use consistent reporting periods.

items.says: The template’s scale or adoption is missing.
items.because: It would show the improvement was not limited to one case.

items.says: The valuation date is missing.
items.because: Market-price proximity needs context.

items.says: The bullet does not clarify what was compared to market price.
Being within 6% of market price should not be presented as independent validation.
items.because: Proximity to market price is not, by itself, evidence that a valuation is accurate.

items.says: “A 1-point change” is ambiguous.
items.because: It should say whether this means a one-percentage-point change in the discount rate.

items.says: The sensitivity test does not identify the starting assumption.
items.because: That would make the USD 52-to-USD 44 range interpretable.

items.says: Your contribution to the pitch or the club’s use of the model is unclear.
The FP&A-support bullet is broad and lacks specific work, scope, or a result.
The team or organization supported is unclear.
items.because: An investment fund’s FP&A work may not be obvious to a reader.

items.says: The performance-report benchmark is unidentified.
items.because: The comparison should be clear.

items.says: The bullet does not say what decisions or analysis the report supported.
items.because: “Every meeting” shows use but not its purpose.

items.says: The cash forecast almost exactly duplicates the Stonebridge result despite the 2018–2019 project dates.
items.because: The overlap makes the later work look backdated.

items.says: The listed methods are broad and should be supported by the experience or projects.
items.because: The technical issues above particularly call financial modeling and DCF valuation into question.

items.says: The presentation could prioritize the finance roles and their strongest, well-supported results.
